**Finding: deviation (critical) — Article XIII, ¶p0130**

The limitation of liability is entirely one-sided:

- **Cap protects only Licensor**, and at "one half of the amount paid by the Licensee" — far below the walk-away floor of six months' fees, and effectively nominal.
- **Licensee is uncapped**, including under the broad Article XII indemnity (which covers Licensee's exercise of the license, its business conduct and any breach of the Agreement).
- **Consequential-damages exclusion runs only in Licensor's favour**, as does a further blanket disclaimer of any IP infringement liability.
- **No carve-outs** for confidentiality/data security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud or IP infringement.

Redline (validated, ok:true) makes the exclusion and cap mutual, resets the cap to the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, inserts an uncapped "Excluded Claims" definition, subjects the IP disclaimer to those Excluded Claims, and confirms our fee obligations are not capped damages. Fallback of a straight 12 months' fees cap is offered in the comment.
